tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index
measurement (SSIM) as global physical metrics.
Sphere volume of interest (VOI) were delineated within targeted organs (liver, kidney and lung). Percentage error
of clinical imaging parameters including SUVmean, SUVmax, total lesion metabolism, as well as the most relevant
radiomics features will be calculated between recovered images to the full-dose images.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

The global physical metrics are used to evaluate the general image quality of recovered imaging, which is standard
criteria in PET image denoising.
The local clinical imaging parameters and radionics features are used to evaluate the recovery of detailed
information and texture.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Team rankings are computed using weighted scores from each evaluation metric. We will calculate measures using
python scripts. Evaluation code will be available together with training dataset so teams can test first.
Particularly, for each individual test subject, weights for different dose reduced factor (DRF) are 5%, 5%, 15%, 20%,
25%, 30% in terms of DRF=2,4,10,20,50,100. As for assessment metrics, 80% weight would be applied to global
metrics (40% for NRMSE, 40% for PSNR and 20% for SSIM), and 20% weight would be applied to local metrics (80%
for SUV parameters and 20% for radiomics parameters).

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

If the submission doesn't include any of the test subject, they are rejected.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The importance of each metrics are different, for example, the global physical metrics would be given bigger
weights compared to local radionics features. Meanwhile, the difficulties and importance of the recovery from
different dose reduced low dose image are different, for example, the larger the reduction factor is, the larger
weight would be given to the score.
